title: Investigation of Flame Retardancy Effect of Licorice Root Extract on Cotton and Cotton-Polyester Blended Fabrics
treatment_chemistry: Licorice-root extract with citric acid and disodium hydrogen phosphate, pH 4, applied by padding
treatment_method: Use the article’s plain-woven substrate. Licorice root of the same batch/lot was prewashed with distilled water; the source additionally says 10 g root was mixed with 300 mL distilled water before oven-drying at 75 °C for 24 h and mechanical cutting. Table 1 extraction uses 5 kg licorice root and 20 L of 99% isopropanol, mixed at 900 rpm for 48 h without air contact, then filtered through Macherey-Nagel MN-GF-3 paper. Heat to 85 °C to remove isopropanol. For the padding bath, Table 2 specifies 12 g extract, 0.6 g citric acid monohydrate, 0.6 g disodium hydrogen phosphate and 250 mL pure water, with acetic acid adjusting pH to 4. The Table 2 heading says Quantity (g/kg), despite those individual amounts and volumes; no concentration denominator is silently repaired. Use the Prowhite horizontal padder with 85% wet pickup, dry at 100 °C for 2 min and cure at 150 °C for 2 min. Generic prose mentions acrylate-copolymer binders in the finishing bath, but the padding recipe lists no binder amount; retain that uncertainty instead of borrowing the coating binder recipe.
LOI_specimen_preparation: Padded fabric strips 52 × 140 mm according to section 3.2, in the initial prepared state. No durability wash is assigned.
TG_locator: Printed p 360, left column, A1 paragraph tied to Figure 8 and B1 paragraphs tied to Figure 10: exact 410 °C rate maximum and state-specific terminal residue.
LOI_locator: Printed p 362, Table 4, exact A1=18.5 and B1=19.3; A1 additionally repeated in following prose.
conditions_locator: Printed pp 354–356, sections 3.1/3.2 and Tables 1/2; local A1/B1 nitrogen attribution p 360. See separately retained source-wide atmosphere discrepancy.
pairing_evidence: Figure 8 explicitly identifies A1 as cotton padded with 12 g licorice extract, and Figure 10 identifies B1 as the corresponding 50% cotton/50% polyester padding state. Local thermal paragraphs name A1/B1 and state N2. Table 4 uses those exact specimen codes for measured LOI. Only initial samples are paired; no washed-state transfer.
source_location: Official 16-page published PDF, printed pp 351–366. Preparation pp 354–356; source-specific N2 and numeric TG p 360; measured LOI Table 4 p 362. Methods/recipe and thermal/LOI page pixels reviewed.
limitations: Two bounded candidates only, pending independent source QA. Canonical nitrogen relies on explicit A1/B1 local result statements together with the N2 method; general air and N2/O2 descriptions remain unresolved and are not erased. The original rate maxima are explicitly 410 °C for both states; terminal residues retain their actual source temperatures, 885 °C and 884 °C, without normalizing to 880 or 900 °C. Do not derive loss fractions or infer missing TG settings. A3 is held for LOI 20.6 Table 4 versus 19.6 prose. B3 residue 8.737% appears in an unlabeled preceding paragraph, so no assignment is made. Controls and all four commercial comparators are reuse-held against the banana study. Recipe concentration wording and unquantified padding binder are preserved; no hidden auxiliaries or source-specific pretreatment borrowed. No LOI/TG replicate count, mean or SD is invented.
